title: Creamy Garlic Chicken Thigh & Mushroom Braise
description: Chicken thighs braised in a Dutch oven with mushrooms and a garlicky chickpea cream sauce, served over quinoa with wilted spinach. About 10g saturated fat for the whole pan.

ingredients.name: extra virgin olive oil, for searing
extra virgin olive oil, for vegetables
low-sodium chicken stock, for chickpea cream
canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed (about half a can)
extra virgin olive oil, for finishing

instructions.text: Soften the chickpeas: Put {10} chickpeas in a small saucepan with {15} baking soda and enough water to cover by an inch. Bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes until very soft and the skins start to slip. Drain and rinse well to remove any soapy baking soda taste. Meanwhile, warm {9} chicken stock in the microwave or a second small pan.

Blend the chickpea cream: While the chickpeas are still warm, blend them with the warm stock, {11} white miso, and {12} lemon juice until completely smooth, 60 to 90 seconds in a high-speed blender. Set aside.

Season and sear the chicken: Pat {0} chicken thighs dry and season with {1} kosher salt and {2} black pepper (hold back a pinch of salt for the vegetables). Heat {3} olive oil in the Dutch oven on induction level 6. Sear the thighs 5 minutes per side until golden. They don't need to be cooked through. Move to a plate.

Cook onion and mushrooms: Drop to level 5. Add {4} olive oil, then {5} yellow onion with a pinch of salt. Cook until translucent, 2 to 3 minutes. Add {6} cremini mushrooms and cook until softened and browned, 4 to 5 minutes. Don't stir constantly; let them sit to brown.
Garlic and tomato paste: Stir in {7} garlic cloves and {8} tomato paste. Cook 1 minute, stirring, until the paste darkens slightly.

Start the quinoa: Rinse {17} quinoa under cold water, then combine with {18} water in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce to a low simmer, and cook 15 minutes. Remove from heat and let steam, covered, until the braise is ready.

Deglaze and braise the chicken: Pour in {16} chicken stock and scrape up the browned bits. Return the chicken and any resting juices, nestling the thighs into the pan. Bring to a gentle bubble, then hold at level 4. Simmer uncovered 10 to 12 minutes, until the thighs reach 165°F. The sauce will be brothy — that's by design.

Add the chickpea cream: Drop to level 2 to 3. Stir the chickpea cream into the pan around the chicken until smooth and heated through, about 1 minute. If it's thicker than you want, loosen with a splash of stock or water.

Wilt the spinach and finish: Stir in {13} baby spinach in handfuls until wilted, about 2 minutes. Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Drizzle with {14} olive oil just before serving. Spoon over quinoa and serve immediately; the sauce keeps thickening as it sits.

notes:
Portions: Dave ~57%, Jen ~43%. Dave's share is roughly 80g protein and ~6g saturated fat.

The sauce is intentionally brothy — it needs the quinoa to absorb into. Without a starch base it eats like a soup.

Leftovers: the sauce tightens in the fridge, so reheat with a splash of stock. Good lunch candidate since it reheats well.
